_note: Mobs that put SEVERAL BODIES WEARING ONE NAME on the field at once.
Reference data about the GAME, like zone_eras.json and reuse_debuffs.json
— never about anybody's raid.
Everything in this parser keys an enemy by NAME, because a name is the
only identity that survives a reparse and the only one comparable between
two guilds' logs. That is exactly right for a boss and exactly wrong for a
mob that splits: two halves each on their own 50s recast interleave into
apparent 25s gaps, and nothing in a log can tell that from one mob on a
25s timer. `aoes.several_bodies` infers it where a reported timer gives it
something to compare against; this file is for the cases where nothing
does — an ability ACT's list has never heard of, or a first pull.
What a name in here BUYS: no learned timer is ever adopted for it, no
config edit is ever suggested for it, and the live panel draws its rows
without a countdown (they still say how many times the ability fired, and
still flash on the landing). Nothing else changes — the audit tab still
lists every cast, and the damage is still the damage.
It is read at RUN TIME by `aoelearn.learn` and the live snapshot, never
baked into a rollup, so adding a name here re-decides every fight the site
already holds without a reparse and without a PARSE_VERSION bump.
`bodies` is how many of that name are up at once when the mechanic has
fully run — a floor and a description, not something any code arithmetics
with. The guard is binary.

A Bisected Rumbler.note: The Segmented Rumbler splits into two of these on death, and each of those splits into three Trisected. Measured on four uploads: `Rumbling of Earth` reads 28.7s across 21 agreeing intervals against ACT's 50s, and the site had ADOPTED that number — two halves alternating, not a fast mob.

A Trisected Rumbler.note: Two Bisected halves make three of these each, so six wear this name at once. Its gaps are the superposition of six clocks and mean nothing at all.
